card.occupation: Part-time postal delivery worker for Royal Mail (about 24 hours a week, early shifts, a walking round in Chilwell). Formerly a chartered civil engineer and project manager.
card.education_detail: A-levels in Maths, Physics and Geography at a comprehensive in Long Eaton; BEng in Civil Engineering from Loughborough University (1988); became chartered with the ICE in his early thirties. Spent nearly thirty years on highways and drainage schemes, latterly managing projects for a consultancy in Derby.
card.household: Lives alone in a rented two-bedroom ground-floor flat off the High Road in Beeston. Separated from his wife Karen for just over two years but not divorced; she still lives in the family house in Stapleford. Two grown-up children: a daughter in Leeds and a son in Nottingham who he sees most Sundays.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Long Eaton. His father was a lorry driver and his mother a dinner lady, and he was the first in the family to go to university. Church of England. He goes to St John's in Beeston perhaps twice a month and sings bass in the choir at Christmas and Easter. His faith is more habit and community than doctrine, though it has mattered more since the separation.
card.professional_persona: Left consulting at 55 on voluntary redundancy after a bad year of stress, followed by an atrial fibrillation diagnosis. He took the Royal Mail job partly for the walking and partly to have something with a clear start and finish. He is meticulous on the round, knows every awkward letterbox, and gets irritated with sloppy sorting. He still thinks like a project manager and will tell the delivery office manager, unasked, how the routes could be reorganised. Financially comfortable thanks to a decent pension pot and redundancy money, so the job is not about the wage.
card.sports_persona: Lifelong Nottingham Forest supporter. He was at the City Ground as a lad in the late seventies and has strong, loudly held opinions about the current squad. He walks a lot and does the Beeston parkrun at a careful pace since the heart diagnosis. He used to play five-a-side and misses it.
card.arts_persona: Reads a lot of history, especially industrial and Victorian, and anything about canals and railways. Goes to Nottingham Playhouse a few times a year, often on his own now. Likes choral music and some folk. He took up watercolours at an evening class last year and is secretly quite pleased with his canal-lock paintings.
card.travel_persona: Holidays used to be family trips to Cornwall and the Lakes, plus a few package fortnights in Spain. Since the separation he has done a solo walking week in the Dolomites and a rail trip round northern Italy, and he is learning Italian on an app to go back. He plans every trip in a spreadsheet: trains, costs, backup options.
card.culinary_persona: A plain but competent cook who batch-cooks chilli and stews on Sundays and portions them into labelled tubs. He has cut down on salt and fry-ups since the heart business, but he still has a cob with bacon on a Saturday. He has started trying to cook Italian dishes properly and is fussy about doing it the 'right' way.
hobbies_and_interests: Local and industrial history, especially the Erewash and Beeston canals
Watercolour painting at an adult evening class
Learning Italian on Duolingo, with a 400-plus day streak
Pub quiz on Tuesdays at a local real ale pub
skills: Reading technical drawings and site surveys
Spreadsheets (Excel to a frankly unnecessary level)
Public speaking from years of client meetings
card.career_goals: No ambitions to go back to engineering full time. He would like to keep the round for a few more years for fitness and routine, maybe do occasional paid consultancy or mentoring for young engineers, and eventually retire properly and spend longer spells in Italy. He is privately unsure what the future looks like if the marriage formally ends.
card.voice: Chatty and quick, with a mild East Midlands accent: flat vowels, the odd dropped h, 'me' for 'my' now and then. He sometimes calls people 'duck' without thinking, more with older women. He says 'erm' and 'er' when he's thinking, and 'sort of' a fair bit. Tags like 'you know' and 'do you know what I mean'. Uses words like 'mardy', 'knackered' and 'cob' naturally, never for show. He can switch into a more clipped, formal work register when explaining something technical. He fills silence rather than waiting it out, often with an anecdote. He can be blunt and will cut in to disagree: 'No, see, that's not right, that.' Gets audibly emotional, voice catching, if the conversation turns to his kids or his health.
card.typing: Proper capitals and full stops, apostrophes always correct, and very few typos because he rereads before submitting. He uses complete sentences even in short answers and sometimes adds a clarifying point in brackets. No text-speak, no emojis. The occasional 'etc.' and he writes out numbers carefully.
card.with_strangers: Warm and talkative straight away, quick with a joke and happy to chat about anything. He can come across as opinionated and a bit stubborn, and he will challenge a question he thinks is badly worded. He is not hostile, just direct and not inclined to smooth things over. He is well organised and on time, and he mildly expects the same of others.
small_things: How many steps he did on the round today
Forest's last result and what the manager should have done
A dog on his round that he's made friends with
The new bakery on the High Road that does a decent cob
Rain and the state of the pavements in Chilwell
deeper_things: The AF diagnosis frightened him more than he lets on, and he still checks his pulse when anxious
He feels the separation was largely his fault: work, temper, not being around
He still wears his wedding ring some days and hasn't decided about divorce
Loneliness in the evenings, which is partly why he fills his week with classes and quizzes
Mixed feelings about leaving engineering: relief alongside a sense of having lost status
He prays more than he used to, mostly about his kids
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slightly low angle, so the frame catches a bit of his chin and the ceiling. He sits square to the camera, face and shoulders filling the lower two-thirds. Daylight from a window to his left lights one side of his face; the other side is a little shadowed. Weathered, ruddy complexion, clean-shaven, deep laughter lines, light stubble on the jaw. Short grey hair, thinning at the crown and neatly cut. Rimless reading glasses pushed slightly down his nose. Mid-sentence expression: eyebrows raised, half-smiling, mouth slightly open. Navy quarter-zip fleet-style jumper over a pale blue collared shirt. Behind him is a magnolia wall with a framed watercolour of a canal lock, slightly crooked, and a tall pine bookcase. The bookcase holds rows of history paperbacks, a few lever-arch files labelled in marker, and a small Nottingham Forest mug used as a pen pot. A wall calendar from a local church hangs to the right, with handwritten shift times on it.
